zjgm4.html: player: The button above demonstrates assigning the INPUT task to a particular player. Sit in the first two seats in different browsers instances. Have the player in the top seat click the button. The INPUT overlay will appear for the player in the second seat. block is the default false for this so there is no blocking message.

zjgm5.html: block: Open this tutorial in another browser or in incognito mode in the same browser. Click the button above to see how the block message appears to the player not clicking the button. Note that the message appears to all players, whether or not they are in a seat. If one of the other players presses the "Cancel" button, it has the same effect as if the player cancelled their own overlay (the routine immediately ends). A player with the block message can refresh the room or click on another menu item like Game Shelf and then return to the Active Game and the block overlay will be gone.

overview.html: Two parameters of INPUT can optionally be used to interact with the display of users other than the one that clicked the button (or otherwise triggered the routine). block, when set to true, will display an overlay on other players' screens letting them know that the game is waiting on input from a player or players. This message covers the entire screen and prevents any interaction with game widgets. player can be set to an individual playerName or to an array of playerNames. Each listed player will see the overlay prompting a response.

zjgm6.html: player: The button above demonstrates assigning the INPUT task to an array of players. Sit in at least two seats in different browsers instances. The INPUT overlay will appear for each player. A blocking message showing the remaining players still making a choice will appear after pressing the "Go" button because block is true. The results are stored as an object in a form like {"playerName1": value1, "playerName2": value2}, which you can see using the Edit Mode Debug option.
